passage: "You said you'd call my parents back. You said it on Tuesday. Do you even care about meeting them, Kaito?" Sami was standing by the counter of their small Toronto apartment, still wearing her work lanyard. Kaito felt the words land one after another like hail. His chest tightened; his mind went blank. He heard himself say, "Can we not do this now," and then he reached for his earphones and turned to the laptop. In his head he was being sensible: no shouting, no fight. Behind him, Sami's voice went up, then stopped. He didn't turn around. He didn't see her sit down on the floor by the counter, staring at the back of his head, feeling more alone than if he had left the room.

qa.q: What had Kaito said he would do?
qa.a: He said he'd call Sami's parents back.

qa.q: What did Kaito think he was doing when he put on his earphones?
qa.a: He thought he was being sensible and avoiding a fight, because his chest was tight and his mind had gone blank.

subtype: Stage 5: Seeing the loop, not the villain [Response]
passage: The power went out at eight, and the rain meant neither of them could go anywhere. Mridul and Sumit sat on the floor of their one-room flat with a single candle and nine per cent battery between their two phones. For once there was no screen to hide in and no door to storm through. After a long quiet, Sumit said, "Can I say something without it being a fight?" Mridul nodded. "When I push you for answers, you go quiet. And when you go quiet, I push harder." Mridul laughed softly. "And then I go even quieter. It's like a machine." "So maybe the machine's the problem. Not you." "Not you either." The candle flickered. Outside, the rain kept on, and for the first time in weeks they were on the same side.

qa.q: How much phone battery did they have between them?
qa.a: They had nine per cent battery between their two phones.

qa.a: It suggests relief and recognition; Mridul sees the pattern too and no longer feels attacked. 🙂

qa.q: Why did the power cut help them see the loop?
qa.a: With no screen to hide in and nowhere to storm off, they had a calm moment to name the pattern together instead of blaming.

qa.q: What changes when Sumit calls the machine the problem?
qa.a: Neither has to be the villain; they stand on the same side against the cycle, which makes the next step possible.

grounding: Shows a couple, in a forced calm moment, naming their press-and-retreat pattern together and treating the cycle, not each other, as the enemy.

subtype: Stage 5: Seeing the loop, not the villain [Response]
passage: On Sunday morning in their Chandigarh flat, with parathas going cold between them, Chandrika pulled a notebook from the shelf. "Can we try something? No blaming." Amandeep eyed it warily. She drew two arrows in a circle. "Here's me asking why you're quiet. Here's you going quieter. Here's me asking louder." He took the pen and added a third arrow. "And here's me finding a reason to go to the gym." They both looked at the page. It was the fight they'd had four times this month, drawn as a loop. "It's not you, exactly," Chandrika said slowly. "It's this." She tapped the circle. Amandeep let out a breath he seemed to have been holding for weeks. "Then let's fight this, not each other."

qa.a: She drew two arrows in a circle.

qa.a: Amandeep would likely have felt blamed and headed for the gym again, restarting the loop instead of stepping out of it.

grounding: Shows a couple calmly mapping their pursue-withdraw pattern together so the cycle becomes the problem rather than either person.

subtype: Stage 6: Softer ask and staying present [Response]
passage: In the break room of the call centre at 2 am, Nusrat found Suraj staring at the vending machine. Last week she would have started with "You never talk to me anymore." Jasleen would tell him something about her day, a funny thing her boss said, a plan for Sunday. He'd say "hmm" or "nice". By Thursday she had stopped telling. I found her in the kitchen, washing the same plate twice. "He doesn't need me here," she said. "I could be a lamp." I don't think Harman knew any of this. I'm not sure I did either, until then.
